title: Convolutions, Kernels, & Feature Maps
description: Discover how 2D convolution filters slide across pixels to detect edges, corners, and texture gradients.

slides.title: The Convolution Operation 🔍
slides.content:
# Sliding Window: The Kernel

A **kernel (or filter)** is a small weight matrix (e.g. $3 \times 3$) that slides across the input image, computing element-wise dot products at each location:

```
Input Image (5x5)            Kernel (3x3)         Feature Map (3x3)
[ 1  0  1  0  2 ]                                
[ 0  3  2  1  0 ]      *     [ 1  0 -1 ]   ==>    [  4   1  -2 ]
[ 2  1  0  2  1 ]            [ 1  0 -1 ]          [  2   0  -3 ]
[ 1  0  2  0  1 ]            [ 1  0 -1 ]          [  5  -1   1 ]
[ 0  1  0  1  0 ]                                
```

### Hyperparameters of a Convolutional Layer:
* **Kernel Size:** Typically $3 \times 3$ or $5 \times 5$.
* **Stride:** How many pixels the filter shifts per step (stride=1 moves 1 pixel at a time).
* **Padding:** Adding border zeros to preserve spatial dimensions (Valid: no padding; Same: preserves dimension).

slides.title: Sobel Edge Detection Kernel in Python 🐍
slides.content: A classic hand-crafted vertical edge detection kernel in Python:
slides.codeSnippet:
import numpy as np

# Sobel vertical edge filter
kernel = np.array([
    [-1, 0, 1],
    [-2, 0, 2],
    [-1, 0, 1]
])

# Vertical boundary image patch
patch = np.array([
    [10, 10, 90],
    [10, 10, 90],
    [10, 10, 90]
])

response = np.sum(patch * kernel)
print('Edge detector response:', response)  # Strong positive signal indicates edge!
